title: Screens per role (UI)
intro: What each person sees first and how the pages are arranged. Asked after every other round, so the answers of rounds 1 to 16 shape these choices.

questions.question: What should a treating doctor see first after logging in?

options.label: One to-do list across patients (Recommended)
options.description: Each row is one next step for one Case File (send 2 requests, re-fetch, approve a resident's draft) with its button; nothing else above it.

options.label: My Case Files with status
options.description: A list of patients with one status each; the doctor opens one to see what to do.

options.label: Next board date first
options.description: The coming board with my Case Files and what each still needs.

options.label: Search box first
options.description: A big UHID or name box, for doctors who come with one patient in mind.

questions.why: Your note on screens: think as a treating doctor, very simple, few clicks. Today the home stacks Case Files, requests, referrals and notifications in sections (DESIGN 7.1, U01). I16 liked; research: 55% of preparation time goes on the system itself (Hartmann 2026).
questions.answer: Neat, filtered Case File list with an urgency tag 1 to 5
questions.own_words: The doctor's first screen should be neat and clean, arranged in a neat order; all Case Files have filters: date, name, treated by, imaging, organ and many more. Each has an urgency tag, a rating from 1 to 5 (5 most urgent): a simple, understandable UI to show all Case Files. They can be cards or list items; you can discuss more or show it directly in the UI mock-up, up to you.
questions.notes: Follow-up needed: who sets urgency (a person, never the AI judging clinical urgency). Show in the mock-up.

questions.question: How should the Case File page be organised instead of today's 7 tabs?

options.label: One page, next step on top (Recommended)
options.description: Header, next-step card, what is missing, records, summary in one scroll; Ask, specialty briefs and audit under a More menu; a loop simply brings its step back to the top.

options.label: Numbered steps (checklist)
options.description: Steps 1 to 5 with ticks; clear the first time, but loops (a new report, a referral) reopen earlier steps.

options.label: Three or four tabs
options.description: For example To do, Records, Summary, Board; less scrolling, one more tap to switch.

questions.why: U16 (seven tabs, jargon on every row), U02 (Case File about 9,500 px tall on a phone), U09 (scroll lost after each action). Your note: the workflow is not linear, it has loops. T16 kept: restructure around what the doctor must do.
questions.own_words: Organise it neat and clear; think in depth about the user experience rather than 'next step on top'; create a new UI / UX component for this, invent something new that doctors and residents use easily, not complex. Ideate with me: first tell me what is there, then take my suggestions.
questions.notes: Moved to a design-together session: research, then the page content inventory, then concepts with the owner.

questions.question: Supporting doctors are already phone-first: which other roles should be designed phone-first?

options.label: Board members joining by code (Recommended)
options.description: Join, current case, call button and the closing pop-up are laid out for a phone first.

options.label: Residents / PG / fellows
options.description: Their Case File work (collecting reports, drafts) is laid out for a phone first.

options.label: Treating doctors
options.description: Home and next steps phone-first; the full Case File stays best on a desktop.

options.label: MDT Coordinator
options.description: Agenda and chasing on the phone; recording the decision stays on a laptop.

questions.why: T17 and I12 settled phone-first for supporting doctors; settled: board members join from anywhere, phone too, with a six-digit code and a call button. Atlas devices: treating doctors OPD desktop and phone, residents ward desktop and phone, coordinator desktop and room screen. What phone members can do comes from R12-Q14.
questions.answer: Laptop first for everyone; phones later
questions.own_words: This is not phone first. Don't make it complex: build for the laptop first; ideally everyone in the hospital has a laptop; then we get to the phone.
questions.notes: Overrides 'phone first' in I12 and T17 and R03 / R17 phone wording: every role laptop-first in the first build.

questions.question: When the next-step card says what to do, what should its button do?

options.label: Finish it in a small panel (Recommended)
options.description: For example 'Send 2 requests' opens both drafts in one panel with one Send; the doctor stays on the page.

options.label: Jump to the right section
options.description: Scrolls to the place on the page where the doctor does it.

options.label: Show the step only
options.description: One line of text, no button; the doctor finds the control.

questions.why: I16 liked: one line saying what to do now. One-panel actions cut clicks (R01 targets). Steps a resident may not do become a send-for-sign-off (R17-Q09).
questions.own_words: First research that UI component in depth, then ask me correctly.
questions.notes: Research launched 17 Oct before asking again.

questions.question: Below one search box (UHID, name, IP / OP No.), how should the treating doctor's Case Files be grouped?

options.label: By who must act (Recommended)
options.description: Needs me, waiting on a department, ready for the board, done; the top group is what to do today.

options.label: By board date
options.description: Upcoming boards nearest first, then Case Files without a date.

options.label: One table with filters
options.description: Sortable columns and filters; powerful, more to learn.

questions.why: U18: no search, names written two ways. Today the list is grouped owned, referred, participating and only asked about (DESIGN 7.1 M3). The coordinator's triage lists (I05) are a separate view (R17-Q11).

questions.question: How should people move between the main areas of the app?

options.label: Phone bottom bar, desktop top bar (Recommended)
options.description: 3 to 5 items per role (for example Home, Case Files, Meetings, Alerts); rare items such as admin and help under the profile menu.

options.label: Left menu plus phone bar
options.description: A left menu on desktop with room for more items, taking width from the Case File; bottom bar on phones.

options.label: Home only, no menu
options.description: Everything starts from home cards; simplest, but more back taps.

questions.why: Today up to 9 buttons sit in the top bar (UI_PLAN A1, A10) and the bar scrolls sideways on phones. Each role sees only its own items (R03).

questions.question: On a desktop, should a list of Case Files stay beside the open Case File?

options.label: No, a quick switcher instead (Recommended)
options.description: The Case File uses the full width; a search box in the top bar jumps to any patient by UHID or name.

options.label: Yes, a narrow list on desktop
options.description: Today's 300 px side list; quick to hop between patients, less room for records.

options.label: Yes, and a drawer on phones
options.description: The same list everywhere; on phones it slides in from the side.

questions.why: Today the 300 px side list sits beside the Case File on desktop and hides behind a button on phones (U02, UI_PLAN A10).

questions.question: Should the Case File show a dated timeline of the patient's records?

options.label: Compact strip above records (Recommended)
options.description: Visits, scans, biopsy and reports as dots on one dated line; tap a dot to open that record.

options.label: As a separate view
options.description: A full timeline one tap away; the main page stays shorter.

options.label: No timeline
options.description: Records stay grouped by OP visit and IP admission, as today.

questions.why: From Dr Minmini's Tempus link (W6): a dated patient timeline is an idea worth borrowing for the screens. Records are already grouped by visit and admission, and a timeline exists on the Board tab (A6). Dates and record names only, no interpretation.

questions.question: Where a resident cannot act (sign, waive, mark ready), what should the screen show?

options.label: 'Send for sign-off' button (Recommended)
options.description: The resident prepares it and sends it; the consultant approves with one tap from their to-do list; the audit shows both names.

options.label: Greyed button with a reason
options.description: Visible but disabled, 'Only Dr X can sign'; the resident tells the consultant outside the app.

options.label: Hidden
options.description: The resident sees only what they may do; cleaner, but they may not know the step exists.

questions.why: Settled: residents join a Case File with a code, have role-based access and cannot sign, 'same as PACS systems'. I03: drafts approved by the consultant, audit shows both names. Which actions are blocked comes from R03 (resident limits) and R06 (team).

questions.question: When a supporting doctor taps a request alert on the phone, what should open?

options.label: The request card itself (Recommended)
options.description: Patient IDs, accession No., what is missing, due date, a link into the RIS / PACS (I14) and the answer button on one screen.

options.label: The department inbox
options.description: The list of all open requests, with the tapped one highlighted.

options.label: The limited Case File view
options.description: The patient's page showing only the items asked about.

questions.why: I12 (phone-first supporting views) and I14 (deep link) liked; U02: the supporting home is about 7,000 px tall on a phone; J2: two systems, no link. The answer steps come from R08 (supporting flow); the alert channel from R14-Q01.

questions.question: How should the coordinator see the Case Files of the next board?

options.label: Columns by triage list (Recommended)
options.description: For discussion, for noting and not ready side by side; each card shows the owner, what is missing and a Remind button.

options.label: One table with readiness
options.description: Rows marked ready, on track, at risk or blocked with chase buttons; today's view, tidied.

options.label: Calendar, then the day's list
options.description: Board dates (per site board) on a calendar; a date opens its agenda.

questions.why: I05 (triage lists) and I06 (cut-off) liked; T13 site boards kept; G22 to G24. Which boards exist and who places a Case File in a triage list come from R10-Q01 and R10-Q11.

questions.question: How should the meeting-room screen be laid out for the current case?

options.label: Case sheet left, record right (Recommended)
options.description: Left: patient line, board question, key values with sources and gaps in large type; right: the record or image being opened; a thin agenda and timer strip at the bottom.

options.label: Full-screen slides
options.description: One section per slide, like the NCG Virtual Tumour Board template; clean, but a record opens as a separate step.

options.label: One large scrolling page
options.description: The presenter scrolls a big-type version of the Case File.

questions.why: I01 presenter mode liked; G25: no presenter view today, and the room page turns into one long column below 1100 px; research: 2 to 6 minutes per case. What the view holds and shows first comes from R12-Q04 and R12-Q05; the timer from R12-Q07.

questions.question: Where should the coordinator type the decision while the room screen shows the case?

options.label: Own laptop, text shown live (Recommended)
options.description: A control view on the coordinator's laptop; the typed decision appears in a strip on the room screen so the board can read it back before saving.

options.label: Own laptop, shown once saved
options.description: The room sees the decision only after it is saved.

options.label: On the room screen itself
options.description: One screen for everything; the case is partly covered while typing.

questions.why: Settled: the coordinator records the decision. Victoria framework: a scribe records in real time and may ask the chair to slow down. Who drives the shared screen and how the wording is confirmed come from R12-Q01 and R13-Q01.

questions.question: How should the root admin's hospital set-up look?

options.label: Short guided steps, then settings (Recommended)
options.description: About 5 steps once (hospital, departments, people, hospital system, board lists), each saved as you go; later a plain settings page.

options.label: One settings page in sections
options.description: Like today but with one Save; quick for experts, hard the first time.

options.label: Set up by the Vaidyx team
options.description: We fill it from a form the hospital sends; admins only manage people.

questions.why: T20 kept: set-up as a short guided flow, department doctors list with confirmation and undo. J4: one long page of separate Save buttons; K07: the live app was never set up. What set-up asks comes from R04 (root admin set-up).
